minted_by.lane: ChatGPT Pro subscription, Sol state worker

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Drivers can improve safety before moving by checking the”.
cards.back: Drivers can improve safety before moving by checking the vehicle, setting the seat and mirrors, fastening restraints, clearing the view and securing carried items.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Underinflated, overinflated or low-tread”.
cards.back: Underinflated, overinflated or low-tread tires can create road-safety problems.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “The handbook recommends checking tire”.
cards.back: The handbook recommends checking tire pressure with a gauge every month.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Use the tire-pressure recommendation on the door-jamb sticker”.
cards.back: Use the tire-pressure recommendation on the door-jamb sticker and check pressure while the tires are cold.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Release air when measured tire pressure exceeds the vehicle”.
cards.back: Release air when measured tire pressure exceeds the vehicle recommendation and add air when it is below that recommendation.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “For the handbook’s tread check, hold a penny by”.
cards.back: For the handbook’s tread check, hold a penny by Lincoln’s body and put his head first into the groove that appears deepest.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Seeing Lincoln’s whole head in the handbook’s penny test”.
cards.back: Seeing Lincoln’s whole head in the handbook’s penny test means the tire is too worn to drive on and should be replaced.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “A driver must ensure that the”.
cards.back: A driver must ensure that the vehicle being driven is safe to operate.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “A poorly maintained vehicle can break down, cause”.
cards.back: A poorly maintained vehicle can break down, cause a crash or leave fewer options in an emergency.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Follow the owner’s manual for routine maintenance, using”.
cards.back: Follow the owner’s manual for routine maintenance, using a qualified mechanic for work that requires one.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Worn or bald tires can lengthen”.
cards.back: Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distance and make wet-road turning harder.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Poor tire balance or low pressure can increase wear,”.
cards.back: Poor tire balance or low pressure can increase wear, reduce fuel economy and make steering or stopping more difficult.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Have a mechanic investigate excessive bouncing, a”.
cards.back: Have a mechanic investigate excessive bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “Worn tires increase the risk of”.
cards.back: Worn tires increase the risk of hydroplaning and of a flat tire.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “The recommended tire pressure in pounds per square inch”.
cards.back: The recommended tire pressure in pounds per square inch is found in the owner’s manual or driver-side door jamb and should be checked with a gauge before entering the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about tires and preparation, beginning with “The second penny-test description calls for replacing a tire”.
cards.back: The second penny-test description calls for replacing a tire when its tread does not reach at least Lincoln’s head with the coin inserted head first.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Have a mechanic inspect brakes that work poorly, make”.
cards.back: Have a mechanic inspect brakes that work poorly, make unusual noise or smells, or have a pedal that sinks to the floor.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights”.
cards.back: Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle to ensure that they work.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Brake lights communicate stopping, while”.
cards.back: Brake lights communicate stopping, while turn signals communicate a turn.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Misaligned headlights may fail to light the”.
cards.back: Misaligned headlights may fail to light the useful area and may dazzle other drivers.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Ask a mechanic to check headlights when night visibility”.
cards.back: Ask a mechanic to check headlights when night visibility is poor or other drivers repeatedly flash their headlights at you.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Replace a damaged windshield because damaged glass may break”.
cards.back: Replace a damaged windshield because damaged glass may break more readily in a minor crash or after an impact.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Keep all installed windshield, rear-window and headlight wipers working,”.
cards.back: Keep all installed windshield, rear-window and headlight wipers working, and replace blades that do not clear water effectively.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Hard steering or a delayed response when the steering”.
cards.back: Hard steering or a delayed response when the steering wheel is first turned requires a mechanic’s steering-system inspection.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “The suspension helps the driver control the vehicle”.
cards.back: The suspension helps the driver control the vehicle and smooths the ride over different road surfaces.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Repeated bouncing after a bump or stop, or difficulty”.
cards.back: Repeated bouncing after a bump or stop, or difficulty controlling the vehicle, can mean the suspension needs a mechanic’s attention.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “The exhaust system reduces engine noise, cools exhaust gases”.
cards.back: The exhaust system reduces engine noise, cools exhaust gases and directs them toward the rear of the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “A leaking exhaust can quickly”.
cards.back: A leaking exhaust can quickly expose vehicle occupants to lethal gases.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Never run a vehicle”.
cards.back: Never run a vehicle engine in a closed garage.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “When sitting in a vehicle with the engine”.
cards.back: When sitting in a vehicle with the engine running for an extended time, open a window.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “Have the exhaust checked periodically because”.
cards.back: Have the exhaust checked periodically because many exhaust leaks cannot be heard.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical roadworthiness, beginning with “A poorly running engine may lose needed power, fail”.
cards.back: A poorly running engine may lose needed power, fail to start or stall, waste fuel and pollute, so follow the owner’s maintenance procedures.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “The windshield and windows forward of or beside the”.
cards.back: The windshield and windows forward of or beside the driver may not have one-way glass, film or another treatment that reduces light transmission below thirty-five percent.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “For rear-window glazing, the handbook prohibits light transmission below”.
cards.back: For rear-window glazing, the handbook prohibits light transmission below twenty percent and states an enforcement tolerance of nine percent.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “A windshield sunscreen device must not”.
cards.back: A windshield sunscreen device must not obstruct or reduce the driver’s clear view.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “The handbook prohibits extending film below the AS-one line”.
cards.back: The handbook prohibits extending film below the AS-one line or below the lowest point of the sun visor.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “Keep the windshield clean and carry cleaner with paper”.
cards.back: Keep the windshield clean and carry cleaner with paper or cloth towels because glare on dirty glass makes seeing harder.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “Keep washer fluid topped up and use antifreeze”.
cards.back: Keep washer fluid topped up and use antifreeze washer fluid when temperatures may fall below freezing.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “Clean inside window surfaces because smoking”.
cards.back: Clean inside window surfaces because smoking can leave a film on the glass.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost from all”.
cards.back: Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost from all windows and clean the vehicle’s front, sides and back.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “Do not hang objects from the mirror or crowd”.
cards.back: Do not hang objects from the mirror or crowd the windshield with decals that can block the view.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about windows and lighting visibility, beginning with “Keep headlights, reverse lights, brake lights and taillights clean”.
cards.back: Keep headlights, reverse lights, brake lights and taillights clean because dirty lenses can reduce their light by fifty percent.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seat and head position, beginning with “Sit upright with the back against the seat and”.
cards.back: Sit upright with the back against the seat and feet on the floor because slouching can reduce restraint effectiveness.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seat and head position, beginning with “Adjust the seat and mirrors before driving to obtain”.
cards.back: Adjust the seat and mirrors before driving to obtain a clear view, full pedal and steering control, and room for the air bag.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seat and head position, beginning with “The driving position should allow the foot to pivot”.
cards.back: The driving position should allow the foot to pivot between brake and accelerator while the heel stays on the floor.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seat and head position, beginning with “The steering-wheel top should stay at or”.
cards.back: The steering-wheel top should stay at or below shoulder height and below the chin.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seat and head position, beginning with “Keep ten inches between the chest and steering wheel”.
cards.back: Keep ten inches between the chest and steering wheel without moving the seat so far forward that steering becomes difficult or reclining the seat.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seat and head position, beginning with “Set the head restraint to touch the back of”.
cards.back: Set the head restraint to touch the back of the head at a height no lower than the ears to help prevent whiplash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mirror setup, beginning with “Adjust the inside mirror to frame the”.
cards.back: Adjust the inside mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mirror setup, beginning with “Set a day-and-night mirror for the time”.
cards.back: Set a day-and-night mirror for the time of day in which you are driving.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mirror setup, beginning with “Set outside mirrors for maximum side”.
cards.back: Set outside mirrors for maximum side and rear visibility and fewer blind spots.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mirror setup, beginning with “To set the left outside mirror using the handbook’s”.
cards.back: To set the left outside mirror using the handbook’s method, rest the head against the closed window and adjust the mirror until the vehicle’s edge is barely visible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mirror setup, beginning with “To set the right mirror, lean until the head”.
cards.back: To set the right mirror, lean until the head is below the inside mirror or above the center console, then adjust until the right vehicle edge is barely visible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mirror setup, beginning with “With that outside-mirror setup, the vehicle sides will not”.
cards.back: With that outside-mirror setup, the vehicle sides will not appear during ordinary mirror glances and each side gains twelve to sixteen degrees of viewing area.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “Always fasten the driver’s seatbelt and”.
cards.back: Always fasten the driver’s seatbelt and ensure passengers use belts or child restraints.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “Seatbelts reduce injury and death risk, help prevent ejection”.
cards.back: Seatbelts reduce injury and death risk, help prevent ejection and help the driver retain control in a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “South Dakota law prohibits driving or riding”.
cards.back: South Dakota law prohibits driving or riding in the front seat without a seatbelt.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “Wear the shoulder belt across the chest and shoulder”.
cards.back: Wear the shoulder belt across the chest and shoulder with little or no slack, never under an arm or behind the back.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “A misrouted shoulder belt can cause”.
cards.back: A misrouted shoulder belt can cause serious internal injury in a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “Fasten the lap belt snugly and low over the”.
cards.back: Fasten the lap belt snugly and low over the hips to reduce the risk of sliding out during a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “Use seatbelts even when”.
cards.back: Use seatbelts even when the vehicle has air bags.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about seatbelts and air bags, beginning with “The handbook describes air bags as protection from striking”.
cards.back: The handbook describes air bags as protection from striking the steering wheel, dashboard or windshield, while warning that they do not provide the cited side, rear or rollover protection or keep the driver behind the wheel in those situations.
